title: Impact of exposure to natural versus urban soundscapes on brain functional connectivity, BOLD entropy and behavior

findings.antecedent: listening to urban sounds compared to nature sounds
findings.consequent: brain entropy (BEN) in posterior cingulate gyrus, cuneus, precuneus, occipital lobe/calcarine
findings.mechanism: listening to urban sounds increases the complexity of the BOLD signal dynamics.
findings.quote: higher BEN was shown when listening to urban sounds as compared to nature sounds

findings.antecedent: listening to urban sounds compared to nature sounds
findings.consequent: functional connectivity (FC) between areas in the auditory, cinguloopercular, and somatomotor hand and mouth networks
findings.quote: lower FC between areas in the auditory, cinguloopercular, and somatomotor hand and mouth networks when listening to urban sounds compared to nature sounds

findings.antecedent: listening to urban sounds compared to nature sounds
findings.consequent: functional connectivity (FC) using the anatomical atlas (AAL)
findings.quote: No robust differences were found using the anatomical atlas (AAL).

findings.antecedent: mean brain entropy (BEN) in PCC, cuneus, precuneus, occipital lobe/calcarine when listening to urban sounds
findings.consequent: change in positive affect (PANAS) from before to after urban sound exposure
findings.mechanism: the higher the BEN, the stronger the decrease in positive affect in the urban sound condition.
findings.quote: We found a negative correlation between the mean BEN when listening to urban sounds and the change in positive affect (PANAS)

findings.antecedent: mean brain entropy (BEN) when listening to urban sounds
findings.consequent: change in negative affect (PANAS), cognitive performance (DNB, DBS, composite score)
findings.quote: No correlations were found with the remaining variables (p-values >0.3).

findings.antecedent: mean functional connectivity (FC) in auditory, cinguloopercular, somatomotor hand and mouth networks when listening to nature sounds
findings.consequent: change in composite cognitive score (Digit span and Nback) from before to after nature sound exposure
findings.mechanism: the higher the FC the higher the increase of the composite score after listening to nature sounds. (Note: The reported r-value of -0.46 contradicts the stated 'positive correlation' if an increase in score is positive.)
findings.quote: a positive correlation between the mean FC when listening to nature sounds and difference (post-pre) of the composite score

findings.antecedent: mean functional connectivity (FC) when listening to urban sounds
findings.consequent: change in composite cognitive score (Digit span and Nback) from before to after urban sound exposure
findings.quote: No significant correlations were found for the urban sound condition.

findings.antecedent: mean functional connectivity (FC) when listening to nature or urban sounds
findings.quote: No correlations were found with the remaining variables (p-values >0.15).

stimuli.description: Forty natural soundscapes (birdsongs, moving water, insects, wind) and forty urban soundscapes (traffic sounds, café ambiance, machinery sounds), each 20s duration with 500-ms linear fade in/out.

limitations: The described correlations (Findings 4 and 6) do not survive multiple comparison correction and therefore need to be treated with caution.

The current study lacks the methodological framework to answer whether experience with nature is beneficial or if experience with urbanicity is detrimental, as resting state brain data was only acquired during the soundscape exposure and not before and after the intervention. Future studies should acquire resting state data before and after natural versus urban soundscape exposure.
